title: Multidistrict litigation
summary: Multidistrict litigation coordinates federal actions pending in different districts that share common factual questions. Under § 1407, the Judicial Panel on Multidistrict Litigation can transfer them for coordinated or consolidated pretrial proceedings.
notes: MDL is distinct from class certification and does not automatically supply subject-matter jurisdiction, merge every action, or bind every plaintiff to a representative judgment. The source’s statistics and practice descriptions reflect its publication period.

sections.Meaning: Multidistrict litigation coordinates federal actions pending in different districts that share common factual questions. Under § 1407, the Judicial Panel on Multidistrict Litigation can transfer them for coordinated or consolidated pretrial proceedings.
sections.How to work through the question: Identify the shared factual questions, the proposed efficiencies, and the distinction between pretrial coordination and trial. Lexecon addresses the statutory duty to remand transferred cases; the chapter also examines management, lead counsel, settlement incentives, and the interests of individual parties.
